en.name: Zha cai
en.summary: Zha cai is the swollen stem of a mustard plant, salted, pressed, fermented and aged before it is sold in vacuum sachets, tins or whole knobs. It is a salt preserve, so an unopened pack sits happily in the cupboard for about 12 months. Once cut open it needs the fridge, where it runs about 2–4 weeks.
en.pantry: Sealed vacuum sachets and tins keep in a cool dry cupboard to the printed date, about 12 months from purchase. The reason they need no refrigeration is the process: the stems are field-dried, salted, turned during fermentation and aged before packing, so the finished product is heavily salted and acidic. Keep packs out of direct sun and away from the cooker, and do not store a pack that has been pierced or has lost its vacuum.
en.fridge: Once the sachet is cut, get the contents into a sealed jar at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use them within about 2–4 weeks. Shredded, seasoned zha cai in oil is the most perishable form on the shelf — it is wet, it has been rinsed of some of its salt, and it moulds at the surface. A whole knob keeps better than shreds, so buy whole and cut what you need. Rinse only the portion you are about to cook, never the whole jar.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for zha cai and freezing is beside the point: salt is already doing the preserving, and the fridge covers the few weeks an opened pack needs. Freezing would also soften the dense, crunchy texture that is the whole reason for using it. If you have more than you can use, buy smaller packs next time rather than filling the freezer.
spoilage: Fuzzy mould at the surface of the jar, especially on oiled shreds
A rotten or yeasty smell rather than the usual salty-sour one
Texture gone soft and mushy instead of dense and crunchy
A swollen sachet or a tin with a bulging end
tips: Buy a whole knob rather than shreds if you use it slowly; it keeps much better.
Decant opened packs into a clean jar — the cut sachet is not a storage container.
Use a dry spoon or chopsticks every time.
Write the opening date on the jar; a couple of weeks passes faster than you think.

faq.q: Does unopened zha cai need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. A sealed sachet or tin keeps in a cool dry cupboard for about 12 months from purchase, because salt and fermentation do the preserving.

faq.q: How long does zha cai last once opened?
faq.a: About 2–4 weeks in a sealed jar at 4 °C or below. Oiled, shredded zha cai is the most perishable form and moulds at the surface.
There is no timeline and no real need. Freezing softens the crunch that is the point of the ingredient.

faq.q: Should you rinse zha cai before cooking?
faq.a: Rinse only the portion you are about to use, to take the edge off the salt. Rinsing the whole jar shortens its life sharply.

zh.name: 榨菜
zh.summary: 榨菜是芥菜膨大的莖瘤，經過鹽漬、壓榨、發酵與熟成之後，以真空包、罐頭或整顆販售。它是鹽漬保存品，所以未開封的包裝放在櫥櫃裡大約可以放 12 個月。一旦剪開就要冷藏，大約 2～4 週。
zh.pantry: 未開封的真空包和罐頭放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃裡，到標示日期為止，從購買日起算約 12 個月。不需要冷藏的原因在於製程：菜頭先日曬、鹽漬，在發酵過程中翻動，再經過熟成才包裝，成品鹽度高、酸度也夠。包裝請避開陽光直射和爐火，已經破孔或真空跑掉的包裝就不要再存放了。
zh.fridge: 包裝一剪開，就把內容物移到密封玻璃罐，放在 4 °C 以下，大約 2～4 週內用完。加了油的調味榨菜絲是架上最容易壞的形式——它含水、部分鹽分已經被沖掉，表面很容易長霉。整顆的比切絲的耐放，所以建議買整顆，要用多少切多少。要煮多少就沖洗多少，千萬不要把整罐都沖過。
zh.freezer: 榨菜沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有意義：鹽已經在做保存的工作，而開封後那幾週冷藏就夠了。冷凍還會讓它那種紮實爽脆的口感變軟，而那正是使用榨菜的理由。用不完的話，下次買小包裝就好，不必塞冷凍庫。
spoilage: 罐口表面長出絨毛狀的霉，尤其是油漬的榨菜絲
聞起來是腐敗味或酵母味，而不是原本的鹹酸味
口感從紮實爽脆變成軟爛
包裝脹袋，或罐頭兩端鼓起
tips: 如果用得慢，買整顆而不是切絲的，耐放很多。
開封後移到乾淨的玻璃罐——剪開的袋子不是保存容器。
每次都用乾燥的湯匙或筷子。
在罐子上寫開封日期；幾週過得比想像中快。

faq.a: 不用。未開封的真空包或罐頭放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 12 個月，因為鹽漬和發酵已經在保存它。

faq.q: 榨菜開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封玻璃罐冷藏在 4 °C 以下大約 2～4 週。加油的榨菜絲最容易壞，會從表面開始長霉。
沒有對應期限，也沒有必要。冷凍會讓爽脆度變軟，而那正是吃榨菜的重點。
只沖要用的那一份，去掉一點鹹味就好。把整罐沖過會大幅縮短保存期。
